Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and G4103; (actively) disbelieving, i.e. without Christian faith (specially, a heathen); (passively) untrustworthy (person), or incredible (thing):--that believeth not, faithless, incredible thing, infidel, unbeliever(-ing).
BiblicalUsage: The unbelieving person, the one without faith. Paul forbids the unequal yoke in 2 Corinthians 6:14 — what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness? — and yet in 1 Corinthians 7:12 he tells the brother whose wife believeth not to keep her if she is pleased to dwell with him. Jesus speaks straight to Thomas in John 20:27, ‘be not faithless, but believing,’ and Revelation 21:8 puts the unbelieving among those whose part is the lake of fire.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word forces me to hold two truths at once: unbelief is a real and damning condition, and the unbeliever in my own house is still someone to love and live with patiently. Paul does not soften the divide, and he does not command me to widen it by leaving. Faith is the line; love is how I stand on my side of it.
